│   │   └── ObjectPool.js          # Generic typed pool (acquire/release/recycle) for projectiles,
│   │                              #   entities, rings — zero allocation in hot paths
│   ├── vfx/                       # The six required VFX systems, all pooled
│   │   ├── ParticleManager.js     # CENTRALIZED. Single InstancedMesh (1 draw call), hard cap 500
│   │   │                          #   live particles, priority-based eviction of oldest, per-instance

│   │   ├── MotionTrails.js        # Pooled ribbon/instanced-segment trails for fast movers (ball, ships)
│   │   ├── ShockwaveRings.js      # Pooled expanding emissive torus/ring meshes on impacts & deaths

│   ├── audio/

│   │                              #   (osc + noise + envelopes), step-sequencer music, master bus
│   ├── postfx/

│   │                              #   owns dispose of passes/composer targets

│   │                              #   tuned for bloom (emissiveIntensity > 1 on emitters only), shared

**Key architectural decisions baked into this structure:**

1. **Simulation/render decoupling.** `Engine` runs a fixed 120 Hz timestep accumulator; render interpolates. This makes collision math deterministic (critical for classic arcade fairness) and gives HitStop a clean seam: it scales the *sim delta*, not the frame rate — the world dilates, the camera keeps breathing.
2. **Ownership boundaries.** Every module that allocates GPU resources owns its `dispose()`. `Engine.teardown()` calls them in reverse construction order; `deepDispose` guards against double-dispose. No global registries of live objects outside the pools.
3. **Particle cap is structural, not advisory.** The 500-particle budget lives in exactly one place — `ParticleManager`, backed by a single preallocated `InstancedMesh`. Spawn requests beyond capacity evict lowest-priority oldest particles; no other system may create particle geometry.
4. **Bloom discipline.** Only designated emitters (ball core, paddles' strike edges, rings, particle sprites) carry `emissiveIntensity > 1`; the rest stay below the bloom threshold (~0.85) so glow reads as light, not a white-out.
5. **Input is one struct.** Keyboard and gamepad both write into the same polled state with edge-triggered events; game code never touches raw `keydown` or `navigator.getGamepads()`.

## Compliance Statements

- **Anti-Lazy Directive:** Acknowledged. Every function in every file will be fully implemented — no placeholder comments, no stubbed branches, no "TODO" escapes. A method that is called must exist and behave; a module imported must export what is consumed. I will self-audit import/export symmetry before declaring any phase complete.
- **Strict Memory Management:** Acknowledged. All projectiles/entities/particles flow through pools (zero steady-state allocation in the hot loop); every geometry, material, texture, composer pass, and audio buffer has an explicit owner that calls `.dispose()` on teardown; `InstancedMesh` is used for particles and any repeated static geometry to keep draw calls flat.
- **Sequential Output Protocol:** Acknowledged. I will not generate beyond the step you have triggered. If any file's output truncates, stop cleanly at the cut point — say **"continue"** and I resume from that exact character with no preamble or restart.
